title: How to Choose an Electrical Box: New Work, Old Work, and Special Cases
summary: This video walks through selecting electrical boxes for common residential applications, contrasting new-work plastic boxes installed on studs with old-work boxes that are fitted after drywall is in place. It covers when to use plastic versus metal boxes depending on cable type, explains grounding considerations for metal boxes, differentiates single-, double-, and multi-gang configurations, and discusses box choices for lighting and ceiling installations (including fan-rated boxes) along with a common bracing approach for walls lacking a stud. The hosts emphasize practical installation steps, compatibility with cable types, and future-proofing for heavier fixtures.

sections.title: New work plastic boxes: purpose and installation
sections.description: Introduces 'new work' construction and plastic boxes used in residential projects. Describes quick installation by nailing the box to a stud, followed by drywall coverage. Notes that some boxes include a nailing flange and embedded nails, and that plastic boxes are common in new construction.

sections.title: Plastic vs. metal boxes and cable-type considerations
sections.description: Discusses choosing plastic boxes for non-metallic (NM) cable and metal boxes for metal-clad cable, highlighting grounding considerations when using metal boxes.

sections.title: Old work vs. new work; install basics
sections.description: Defines old work vs. new work concepts. Describes installing an old-work plastic box by cutting drywall, sliding the box in, and tightening screws to engage a clamp to hold it in place.

sections.title: Box sizes and configurations: 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-gang; round vs. rectangular
sections.description: Outlines common gang configurations and their applications (lights, switches). Explains that round boxes are typically used for lighting and outlines the variety of sizes available to fit different wiring layouts.

sections.title: Ceiling and lighting considerations: fan-rated and future-proofing
sections.description: Covers use of boxes for ceiling installations, recommending metal boxes for heavier fixtures or future upgrades (e.g., ceiling fans). Explains that a fan-rated box is mounted to structure to carry additional weight and accommodate future fixtures.

sections.title: Non-standard mounting: brace-in-box solutions for hollow walls
sections.description: Describes a brace-style box (toggle/brace) that expands and tightens against the wall structure to support the box when there is no stud in the correct location, enabling the box to carry heavier fixtures.

sections.title: Wrap-up and practical note
sections.description: Hosts encourage applying what was shown, suggest exploring more videos for home improvement guidance, and invite viewers to subscribe for new content.
